messages.subject: ctrl + arrow keys to jump words not working in R console launched from Nvim-R
messages.subject_clean: ctrl + arrow keys to jump words not working in R console launched from Nvim-R
messages.body_plain:
work flow:

1. nvim [nameof file].R
2. ,rf   [, is local leader]
3. ctrl + w, ctrl + w
4. i, to go to insert mode
5.  type a vector of numbers
6. press ctrl + left arrow (or right) to jump through the vector values, as I would with the normal R console

ctrl+ arrow is producing strange output on the console line (as shown in the attached file, little diamonds with ? on it).

How can I resolve this and get expected behaviour?
I would take an educated guess that this is not related to my tmux configuration, but something to do with the terminal configuration in nvim.

i've tried experimenting with the options in section 6 of the documentation (https://github.com/jalvesaq/Nvim-R/blob/master/doc/Nvim-R.txt),
including the part in 6.2 with let R_term = "xterm", but this has not resolved the problem.

I notice that when in insert mode, ctrl + v, then pressing the left arrow produces  ^[[D, and for right ^]]C.  Tab does not work either.  I've tried  unsuccessfully remapping keys as you might in vim when ctrl + arrow doesn't work( googling on the net for how to do that).  I'm stuck!

Any ideas on how I can quickly jump through text (to edit cells of a vector say) I write in the R console when launching it with nvim-R?

PS thanks to the author for making such a great package for developing in with R!

messages.body_plain:
Sorry, but the plugin was designed since the beginning with the goal of helping the development of R scripts. We can only start R from Neovim, not the other way around. What you can do is save the history with savehistory(), quit R and, then, start editing the saved history with Neovim.

What is your terminal emulator? I can't see the behavior that you describe in any circumstance. When I press Ctrl+Arrow, I get:

xterm, st and gnome-terminal: ;D for left arrow and ;C for right arrow.
Tmux: Regardless of using st, xterm or gnome-terminal, the Ctrl key is ignored, and the cursor moves 1 column (left or right).
Neovim terminal: Regardless of being in Tmux or not, I see the diamonds as in your screenshot.

Tab works for me in Neovim terminal. For example, if I press `ls(<TAB>`, I get:

> ls(
name=       pos=        envir=      all.names=  pattern=    sorted=
> ls(

I don't understand that much of terminals. My ~/.inputrc is from 2011, and its content is:

set visible-stats on
set editing-mode on
set keymap vi
set bell-style audible

I don't remember from where I copied these lines... I also have this in my .bashrc:

set -o vi

Perhaps you have an option set in your .tmux.conf that makes the cursor jumping one word with Ctrl+arrow...

messages.subject: Vim-R-plugin 1.3.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Version 1.3.0 was released.

The changes are:
Delete option vimrplugin_restart.
Set the environment variable R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES which makes it unnecessary to have the command library(vimcom) in Rprofile.
Use the +channel and +job features instead of +clientserver. This means that it is no longer necessary to start Vim with the --servername argument, and the communication with R works even if the X server is not running (like in a remote session through ssh without the -X argument or in Mac OS X without X Quartz running).
Requires Vim >= 7.4.1425.

messages.subject: Re: Vim-R-plugin 1.3.0 released
messages.body_plain:
You can find installation instructions in the plugin's documentation, available at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin/master/doc/r-plugin.txt

If you are going to use Vim-R-plugin, you have to install vimcom, setwidth, colorout, and tmux. And you have to edit your ~/.Rprofile and ~/.tmux.conf.

However, if you use Neovim and the development version of Nvim-R, you don't need Tmux. Then, the installation instructions for Vundle is simply:

Plugin 'jalvesaq/Nvim-R'

No other configuration is mandatory.

messages.subject: Vim-R-plugin was replaced by Nvim-R
messages.body_plain:
Details on the replacement are explained at https://github.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin/issues/204

On Windows, users have two options:
Use the released versions of Nvim-R and nvimcom, both available at Nvim-R/releases <https://github.com/jalvesaq/Nvim-R/releases> (note that nvimcom is released only when needed and currently the last nvimcom binary (0.9-14) was released with Nvim-R 0.9.2).
Install the development version of Nvim-R and install Rtools <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/> to be able to build nvimcom yourself.
